checklist.detail: Report available core/delay estimates, mass effect, hydrocephalus and relevant alternative diagnoses.

measurements.name: ASPECTS
measurements.method: For an applicable MCA-territory examination, record modality, side and affected regions; score 10 minus affected regions.
measurements.pitfall: Do not apply MCA ASPECTS to posterior circulation or treat a score as an independent treatment decision.

measurements.name: Perfusion volumes
measurements.method: Record software, thresholds, estimated core and delayed tissue in mL, mismatch volume and ratio if valid.
measurements.pitfall: Motion, poor bolus, truncation and reperfusion can invalidate estimates.

classification.name: ASPECTS
classification.version: 10-region MCA score; name CT or DWI application
classification.applicability: Anterior-circulation ischaemic change in the MCA territory.
classification.summary: Record the affected regions with the score. Posterior circulation and perfusion use separate assessments; the score does not alone determine treatment.

steps.label: Parenchyma and ASPECTS
steps.detail: Look for early ischaemic change and localise it by side, territory and strategic structures; give ASPECTS when applicable.
findings: Loss of the insular ribbon and obscuration of the [left] lentiform nucleus; ASPECTS __ (regions [ ]).
Established hypoattenuation in the [right] MCA territory.
Restricted diffusion in the [ ] with low ADC (acute infarct).
steps.look: Narrow window width (about 30–40 HU) on non-contrast CT: insular ribbon, lentiform nucleus and cortex; DWI with ADC on MRI.
steps.tip: A normal early CT does not exclude infarction; subtle loss of grey–white differentiation needs a narrow window.

steps.label: Haemorrhage
steps.detail: Exclude intracranial haemorrhage in every compartment before treatment decisions.
findings: Haemorrhagic transformation of the infarct [petechial / parenchymal haematoma].
steps.look: Parenchyma, subarachnoid spaces, ventricles and extra-axial spaces on non-contrast CT or susceptibility MRI.

steps.label: Arterial occlusion
steps.detail: Name the occluded artery and segment, tandem cervical disease and distal reconstitution.

normal.ARTERIAL FINDINGS: No large-vessel occlusion; cervical and intracranial arteries patent.

findings: Occlusion of the [left] M1 segment of the MCA (dense MCA sign on non-contrast CT).
Tandem occlusion: [right] ICA origin and M1.
Cervical ICA dissection with tapered narrowing.
steps.look: CTA from the arch to the vertex; dense artery sign on non-contrast CT.
steps.tip: Look at the cervical arteries too: a tandem ICA lesion changes the endovascular approach.

steps.label: Collaterals and perfusion
steps.detail: Describe collateral filling and, when valid, perfusion core and hypoperfused tissue volumes with the software used.
findings: Good collaterals: filling of more than half of the territory with a one-phase delay.
Perfusion ([software], thresholds [ ]): core __ mL, hypoperfused tissue __ mL, mismatch volume __ mL.
steps.look: Multiphase CTA for delayed collateral filling; perfusion maps checked for motion, bolus and coverage.
steps.tip: Single-phase CTA underestimates delayed collaterals; treatment selection follows the clinical pathway, not a single number.

steps.label: Mass effect and alternative findings
steps.detail: Report oedema, midline shift, cisterns, hydrocephalus and any alternative diagnosis.

normal.MASS EFFECT AND OTHER FINDINGS: No mass effect; no alternative cause for the symptoms.

findings: Malignant oedema with __ mm midline shift and effacement of the basal cisterns.
Cerebellar infarct compressing the fourth ventricle with early hydrocephalus.
steps.look: Midline, basal cisterns and fourth ventricle (for cerebellar infarcts).
